header.title: How to Replace a Refrigerator Start Relay
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to replace a refrigerator start relay, ensuring your appliance can efficiently restart its compressor.

steps.description: The first step is to disconnect the refrigerator from the power supply to prevent electrical shock.
actions: Unplug the refrigerator from the wall
Turn off the circuit breaker for the refrigerator

steps.description: Wear safety gear like insulated gloves and safety glasses when working with electricity.
actions: Wear insulated gloves
Wear safety glasses

steps.description: Remove the refrigerator panel by loosening or removing screws.
actions: Locate refrigerator panel
Loosen screws
Remove screws

steps.description: This step involves locating the refrigerator capacitor and safely disconnecting its leads to prevent electrical shock.
actions: Confirm if a capacitor is present.
Locate the capacitor (tube-like part with wiring attachments to the compressor and relay).
Remove the leads from the resistor part.
Attach the leads onto the leads of the capacitor.

steps.description: This step involves locating and removing the relay terminal cover to access the start relay.
actions: Determine the location of the relay terminal cover.
Locate the relay terminal cover by the lower interior part at the back portion of the refrigerator.
Identify a wire connecting to the cover from the compressor.
Take out the relay terminal cover.
Find the start relay directly underneath the cover.
Observe wires plugged into the relay terminals.
Observe a spool of copper wires wrapping the relay.
Take out the copper wires by pulling the connector attached to the relay.

steps.description: This step involves replacing the start relay, connecting wires, and reinstalling components to restore refrigerator functionality.
actions: Find a start relay at appliance or hardware stores.
Connect the wire back to the new starter relay.
Install the new relay back to the connectors.
Put the terminal cover back on.
Return the cover panel of the refrigerator back on.
Plug the refrigerator back in.
